card.title: Hand It Over
card.instruction: Persuade someone to give up control of a task, object, or decision you believe is being mishandled.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let me fix that cupboard hinge. The door's lower than when you started.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm just finding the right screw.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've tried four. Give me the screwdriver while you find it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then you'll tell everyone you fixed it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can announce the repair. I'll stand behind you with the screwdriver, keeping the door attached.

mechanism: A seeks the screwdriver and repair control while offering B public credit to remove the obstacle to handover.
confusable: Unlike merely criticizing a repair, A must negotiate possession of the task being mishandled.
comparison: D36-a exchanges announcement credit for tool control; D36-b promises to preserve effort while taking the seating-plan pencil.
provenance: Direct local assistant candidate preparation; not fresh review or acceptance.
